notes:
RESIDENTS
Source: STATISTIK AUSTRIA, register-based population grid (Regionalstatistische
Rastereinheiten), INSPIRE 100 m ETRS89-LAEA mesh, reference date 2026-01-01.
Measured register counts per cell, not estimates or model output. 588,886
populated cells nationally; 28,114 fall inside the map bbox, carrying 2,274,209
residents. That exceeds Vienna's own population (2,022,557) because the map bbox
is a rectangle extending into Lower Austria to reach Flughafen Wien-Schwechat.

Suppression check, as the submission guide recommends: the 100 m table sums to
9,215,956 residents nationally, against a published Austrian total of ~9.19
million. Agreement well inside 5%, so no material suppression at this grain.

Note this is NOT the OGDEXT_RASTER_1 dataset, which publishes grid geometry only
and carries no population attribute.

Cells were aggregated upward from 100 m to ~300 m demand blocks placed at the
activity-weighted centroid of their constituent cells. No downward spreading was
performed: the published grain is finer than the map's demand points, so there is
no placement step on the residence side. Cells are clipped to the map bbox in
WGS84 rather than in LAEA, so no demand falls outside the playable area.

WORKPLACE
Total is published: STATISTIK AUSTRIA, Abgestimmte Erwerbsstatistik 2024,
Erwerbstaetige am Arbeitsort, Wien = 1,111,548 jobs. Of those, 284,847 are
Einpendler:innen commuting in from other Bundeslaender (Niederoesterreich
207,177; Burgenland 25,081; Steiermark 16,315; Oberoesterreich 15,201; Kaernten
6,860; Tirol 6,519; Salzburg 5,538; Vorarlberg 2,156). Those enter the map
through seven outside-connection corridors rather than as internal jobs.

The remaining 826,701 are people who both live and work in Vienna - equal to the
city's 938,544 employed residents minus 111,843 out-commuters, which the
published table confirms exactly. That figure is what the gravity model
distributes.

No free official workplace grid exists for Austria: the Statistik Austria
Arbeitsstaetten and employment rasters are paywalled (EUR 354 base fee per order,
with only >=10 km grids partly free). The published city-wide total is therefore
distributed across OpenStreetMap office, retail, industrial, institutional,
education and healthcare features using generic European per-type employment
densities - a building-type dasymetric with non-locally-calibrated weights.
44,825 workplace features resolved to 11,006 100 m cells. Footprints are OSM, not
a cadastre.

So the workplace TOTAL is measured and citable at municipality grain; its
PLACEMENT within the city is modelled. The per-corridor split of the 284,847
in-commuters across the seven corridors is likewise modelled, weighted by rail
and road corridor capacity - only the total is published.

COMMUTE FLOWS
Not observed. Flows come from a doubly-constrained gravity model (Furness/IPF
balancing, exponential distance decay, beta = 0.16), calibrated so the modelled
commute distribution matches Vienna's published median commute.

For transparency: Statistik Austria does publish origin-destination commuter
tables in the Abgestimmte Erwerbsstatistik, but only between Bundeslaender
(ADM1). Vienna is a single Bundesland, so that table constrains flows entering
and leaving the map - which is how the corridor totals above were set - and says
nothing about movement between points inside the city. Intra-city flows are
therefore fully estimated.

Pops are sampled proportional to modelled flow rather than truncated to each
origin's strongest destinations, so the emitted file reproduces the model's own
concentration profile instead of collapsing demand onto a handful of points.

ROUTING AND GEOMETRY
Driving times and distances routed with OSRM over the OpenStreetMap road network.
Map geometry built with depot. Buildings from Overture Maps release 2026-07-22.0.
Of ~340,836 footprints only 39.1% carried a height and 13.4% a usable floor
count, so heights were imputed in three tiers: real height, then floors x 3.2 m,
then the median height of buildings in the same ~150 m cell, falling back to
~750 m and finally the city median. Validated on the 18,951 buildings carrying
both attributes: implied metres per floor 3.22 median against the 3.2 assumption.
Every building carries a height_source property recording which tier produced it.

SPECIAL DEMAND (not scored, cited for completeness)
Flughafen Wien-Schwechat, 18 university and Fachhochschule campuses, 12 major
hospitals, 23 venues / retail / government sites, and the seven
outside-connection corridors above. Coordinates hand-curated from
OpenStreetMap. Ferry demand deliberately excluded.

VINTAGES
Residents: reference date 2026-01-01.
Employment and commuting: Abgestimmte Erwerbsstatistik 2024.
Buildings: Overture release 2026-07-22.0.
Road network and POIs: OpenStreetMap extract, August 2026.

Workplace source note: the Abgestimmte Erwerbsstatistik is a register-based
census - place of work is established by linking administrative registers, not
estimated from population. The figure used (1,111,548 Erwerbstätige am Arbeitsort,
Wien 2024) is a direct job count, published at municipality grain.

O/D note: the corridor volumes entering the map are set from published measured
in/out commuter totals for Wien (284,847 in, 111,843 out). Flows between points
inside the city remain fully estimated by the gravity model.
